r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency graph and recent deployments/changes for orders-service, mobile-bff, payments-api, upi-gateway, and portfolio-service. Orders-service directly depends on mobile-bff (upstream), and calls broker-api and portfolio-db (downstream). Several deployments and changes occurred prior to the incident, including a push notification campaign at 13:30.

findings.statement: orders-service depends on mobile-bff upstream and calls broker-api and portfolio-db downstream.
market-data-service and user-db were deployed shortly before the incident at 12:39 and 12:40 UTC on 2026-10-10.
A push campaign 'diwali_sip_offer' was sent to 2.1M users via notification-service at 13:30 UTC on 2026-10-10.

open_questions: Did the push campaign at 13:30 trigger a sudden traffic surge that overwhelmed broker-api or orders-service?
Were error rates on broker-api elevated concurrently with the start of order placement failures?

r1-observability-1.summary: Investigation into orders-service and mobile-bff reveals that traffic surges and error spikes began abruptly at 13:31-13:32 UTC on 2026-10-10. orders-service became saturated due to an overwhelmed order-executor queue (capacity 500) resulting in RejectedExecutionException errors, high CPU, and an error rate peak around 15.85%. mobile-bff experienced a corresponding error rate increase peaking at 4.42%.

findings.statement: orders-service traffic (RPS) and CPU usage showed an anomaly starting at 2026-10-10T13:31:00+00:00.
orders-service error rate and p99 latency anomalies began at 2026-10-10T13:32:00+00:00, with error rates peaking at 15.85%.
orders-service logs show RejectedExecutionException: order-executor queue full (capacity 500) starting at 2026-10-10T13:32:04+00:00.
mobile-bff RPS anomaly started at 2026-10-10T13:31:00+00:00 and error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-10T13:32:00+00:00.
mobile-bff logs show retry warnings to payments-api at 13:32:26 UTC and aa-connector at 13:35:21 UTC.
orders-service autoscaler reached its max replicas (6/6) at 13:50:19 UTC.

open_questions: What caused the sudden incoming traffic surge (RPS spike) across mobile-bff and orders-service at 13:31 UTC?

r2-observability-1.summary: notification-service experienced no distress, errors, resource saturation, or latency spikes between 13:30 and 13:35 UTC during the diwali_sip_offer campaign dispatch.

findings.statement: notification-service rps, error_rate_pct, latency_p99_ms, cpu_pct, mem_pct, and pod_restarts showed no anomalous behavior or spikes around 13:30 to 13:35 UTC.
notification-service produced zero WARN or ERROR logs and successfully processed normal informational messages and push campaign dispatches during the window.

hypotheses.title: Push Notification Campaign Overwhelms Orders Service Queue
hypotheses.mechanism: A push notification campaign targeting 2.1M users with a direct deep link to create new SIP orders generated an instantaneous surge in traffic across mobile-bff and orders-service at 13:31 UTC. Although notification-service itself operated successfully without errors or resource saturation, the massive broadcast drove a synchronized flood of incoming user requests that overwhelmed the orders-service executor queue capacity of 500, leading to RejectedExecutionException errors, high CPU utilization, and transaction failures.

supporting.note: Push campaign 'diwali_sip_offer' sent to 2.1M users at 13:30 UTC with deep link to orders/new-sip directly precedes the traffic surge.
mobile-bff traffic spiked abruptly starting at 13:31 UTC, rising from baseline 1097 req/s to 2516+ req/s.
orders-service traffic surged simultaneously at 13:31 UTC, jumping from baseline 115 req/s to 748+ req/s.
orders-service CPU usage spiked from 27.42% to 89.09% starting at 13:31 UTC.
orders-service logged RejectedExecutionException: order-executor queue full starting at 13:32 UTC.
orders-service error rate spiked to 14.12% starting at 13:32 UTC, correlating with the executor queue saturation.
notification-service RPS remained stable without anomalies during the campaign.
notification-service error rate remained at 0.31% with no errors.

assumptions: The push notification deep link successfully drove a large synchronized influx of users to open order forms simultaneously.

hypotheses.title: Routine Deployment of Market Data Service or User DB Triggered Upstream Instability
hypotheses.mechanism: Deployments on market-data-service and user-db shortly before the incident introduced latent bugs or performance degradation that eventually surfaced as high latency and request rejections.

contradicting.note: A 50-minute delay between deployments and the abrupt 13:31 UTC traffic surge without prior anomalies makes a deployment regression far less likely than the direct push campaign trigger.
Traffic metrics show an explicit volume spike starting precisely at 13:31 UTC, matching the push notification timing rather than a gradual deployment degradation.

assumptions: The deployments caused an internal bottleneck that happened to manifest only when traffic levels changed.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: We established the symptom onset at 13:31 UTC based on simultaneous RPS anomalies on mobile-bff and orders-service. Full metrics and logs for notification-service confirm that it remained healthy (zero errors, stable CPU/memory and RPS) while successfully dispatching the push campaign (chg-9674) at 13:30 UTC. This campaign provided an exact causal trigger for the traffic surge, leading directly to queue saturation and RejectedExecutionException errors in orders-service (log-00593). Alternative deployment hypotheses (chg-9148, chg-9417) remain much less likely due to temporal distance and lack of correlation.
